column1: # THE WORKING COPY — this file at the art library root is the list the owner works from. The suite regenerates it (and a mirror under build/_image-prompts/) via npm run art-worklist in the suite repo; edit nothing by hand.
# ART WORK LIST — generated by `node tools/gen-art-worklist.mjs` (npm run art-worklist). Regenerate rather than editing by hand.
# FILENAMES USE HYPHENS (thri-kreen.webp) — NOT underscores (thri_kreen.webp). The sidecar wiring keys art to hyphenated entry-key slugs; a file named with underscores will never be found.
# The filename is the slug of the document key (flags.<module>.key after the last dot) + .webp — never the build/ JSON filename, which can disagree with it.

# The full save path opens every notes cell — every path points into the standalone art library (C:/Projects/FoundryVTT/DakksUltimateTokens/art/<kind-dir>/<slug>.webp). The library is edition-agnostic: the SAME slug reached from two packs or modules is ONE shared file, and the notes name every entry it serves.

# THE LOOP: generate a batch -> save each file at the exact path in its notes cell -> npm run build in the suite (the build resolves library art by existence; a misnamed file silently does nothing — check the name against this CSV) -> reload Foundry.
# Creature tokens: PNG with alpha first, verify per IMAGE-BRIEF.md §9, then convert to .webp. Sizes: Tiny–Large 512px, Huge 1024px, Gargantuan 1536px.
# P1 = generate first (this module). P2 = later. P3 = a real library icon already exists — only for a unified look.

# emblem = non-physical subject rendered as an item-icon-style sigil/effect; not in the original six kinds, added for full coverage (spells, proficiencies, skills, abilities, tables, journals). Classes are kind 'npc' (class portrait — archetypal member).

# CANON BACKLOG rows (kind monster, P3, no suite slot yet) merge the 5e SRD monster list (CC-BY mechanical fields only) with the Too Many Tokens name list (names only), deduped against our own creature rows — art pre-made for future campaigns/editions.
